messages.author: 36bb4216bf88ac1c
messages.subject: Pseudo R2 with multiple predictors
parts:
Hello all,

I was asked to report pseudo-R2 values for two SEM models that have an observed binary outcome. lavaan provides a pseudo-R2 value that I believe is based on McKelvey & Zavoina (1975). If possible, I would like to provide bootstrap-based confidence intervals for the pseudo-R2 values. To do this, my plan is to calculate the pseudo-R2 estimate as a parameter in my lavaan model code and then use the boostrapLavaan() function to calculate confidence intervals. But I don't think that I am calculating the pseudo-R2 statistic properly when there are multiple predictor variables. 

I used the formula provided in equation 15 of the Mplus Technical Appendixes: R2 = [pi^2 * V(x)] / [pi^2 * V(x) + V(delta)], where pi = regression coefficient associated with predictor variable x, and delta = the residual for the latent continuous response variable y* underlying the observed binary outcome y. I believe that Var(delta) = 1 when using probit regression. 

Here is a reproducible example of what I would like to do. Borrowing code from Rosseel (2014), I created a binary version of the Holzinger & Swineford data (code in blue and output in red):

> library(lavaan)

> HS9 <- HolzingerSwineford1939[,c("x1","x2","x3","x4")]
> HSbinary <- as.data.frame( lapply(HS9, cut, 2, labels=FALSE) )

Here is the observed variance-covariance matrix for the data set.

> cov( HSbinary )
           x1           x2                x3                x4
x1 0.22790698 0.04255814 0.05806202 0.05333333
x2 0.04255814 0.25036545 0.06019934 0.05238095
x3 0.05806202 0.06019934 0.23526024 0.03523810
x4 0.05333333 0.05238095 0.03523810 0.24571429

When I treat x1 as binary outcome with a single binary predictor (x2), I can create a new parameter 'r2' that is the same as the lavaan pseudo-R2. Note, I had to provide the variance for the x2 predictor in the formula.

> model1 <- '
> x1 ~ g1*x2
> num := (g1^2)*0.2503654
> den := num + 1
> r2 := num/den
> '

> summary( fit1 <- lavaan( model1, estimator = 'wlsmv', data = HSbinary, ordered = 'x1' ), rsquare = T )

R-Square:
                   Estimate
    x1                0.051

Defined Parameters:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
    num               0.054    0.035    1.540    0.124
    den               1.054    0.035   30.227    0.000
    r2                0.051    0.031    1.623    0.105

However, when I have multiple predictors, my pseudo-R2 estimate is off (lavaan's pseudo-R2 = 0.127 and my version = 0.108). The equation provided in the Mplus Technical Appendixes is for a single predictor and I don't think my attempt to generalize this to the case of multiple predictors was successful. My guess is that this is because the predictors are correlated. 

> model2 <- '
> x1 ~ g1*x2 + g2*x3
> num := (g1^2)*0.2503654 + (g2^2)*0.2352602
> den := num + 1
> r2 := num/den
> '

> summary( fit2 <- lavaan( model2, estimator = 'wlsmv', data = HSbinary, ordered = 'x1' ), rsquare = T )

R-Square:
                   Estimate
    x1                0.127

Defined Parameters:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
    num               0.121    0.050    2.414    0.016
    den               1.121    0.050   22.417    0.000
    r2                0.108    0.040    2.705    0.007


Is anyone able to help me reproduce lavaan's pseudo-R2 value in the case of multiple predictors? 

Many thanks,

-Steve

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Pseudo R2 with multiple predictors
parts: I don't think my attempt to generalize this to the case of multiple predictors was successful. My guess is that this is because the predictors are correlated.

Correct!  The explained variance with 2 correlated predictors must also account for (twice) the covariance:

num := (g1^2)*0.2503654 + (g2^2)*0.2352602 + 2*g1*0.06019934*g2
